title: First deterministic native-world epoch through the PostgreSQL path
objective: A native R-EP runtime over the primary substrate's world (wforge Encounter, design v0.3 s8) with exact checkpoint/restore conformance (k chained epochs == one monolithic run), driven by a fixed deterministic policy that never takes an unaffordable action (so the F09 path is not exercised; wforge's world.py hash is part of the spec); then one native chain through Fabric claim -> approved execution -> PostgreSQL publication -> independent replay -> durable receipt (-> the lake).
problem: The path is qualified on synthetic busy-work only; native epochs need a runtime whose checkpoint captures the whole world state, or chained epochs silently diverge from the world they claim to run.
non_goals: any change to wforge (owner: see the F09 handoff)
evidence_required: RED conformance tests before the runtime
a native chain published, validated by replay on another host, receipted

acceptance.condition: conformance tests green (chained == monolithic, cross-process determinism, F09 path never taken); one native chain through the real path with its receipt
